findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events.
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 
Observed that facility does not have written procedures for Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events(Norovirus) and also does not have proper chemical to assist with cleaning a norovirus event. PIC was made aware and written procedures was provided by inspectors and PIC assured that facility will purchase EPA certified bleach soon. Ensure that having proper EPA certified chemical and written procedures are available to respond to a vomit/diarrheal event. 

Clean-up of Vomiting and Diarrheal Events. A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
4-703.11(C) 
REPEAT
The sanitizer bucket in the front side near soda machine tested at 0ppm (chlorine).The facility has QUAT available and the bucket was remade and tested at 400ppm(quat). Ensure that sanitizer solutions are tested after they are prepared to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized properly.
findings.citation_text: 4-703.11(C)(2) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations, including the application of SANITIZING chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPAregistered label use instructions by providing: (2) A contact time of at least 7 seconds for a chlorine solution of 50 MG/L that has a PH of 10 or less and a temperature of at least 38°C 100°F) or a PH of 8 or less and a temperature of at least 24°C (75°F).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) 
Observed dish machine sanitizing at 0 ppm (Chlorine)after multiple tries and sanitizer bucket was changed by PIC however, still concentrating at 0 ppm. PIC was made aware and called for service immediately. Ensure that the dish machine is functioning properly to be sure that food contact surfaces are getting sanitized.

Additionally, inspectors observed pink colored accumulation on the interior surface of the ice machine. PIC was informed. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned and are always in good condition. 

Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment:
7-201.11
Observed all purpose chemicals and glass cleaner found on food prep tables within the dish room and kitchen area. PIC was informed and chemicals were removed and placed in the appropriate designated area. Ensure that toxic chemicals are stored separately away from food. 

Separation. Poisonous or toxic materials shall be stored so they can not contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single-service and single-use articles by: (A) Separating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS by spacing or partitioning; and (B) Locating the POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS in an area that is not above FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE or SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 
REPEAT 
(1) The following areas are in need of a deep cleaning:
- Surfaces inside and outside of the dish machine
- Each basin of the triple sink has dried food debris
- Floors, walls, and the ceiling behind pieces of equipment inside of the dish room and the kitchen were observed with splatter and accumulated debris 
- Deep cleaning needed in dry storage underneath and behind the storage rack
Ensure that physical facilities are cleaned as often as necessary to prevent debris accumulation.

(2) Observed coving coming out off the wall in between cooking oven and prep cooler. PIC was informed. Ensure that cove base is glued back to the wall to avoid food build up.

Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Several different TCS foods such as but not limited to cheeses and meats lacked proper date marking. These items were stored inside of the prep cooler in the pizza room. Discussed with PIC and the date of preparation was added to the food items. Ensure that TCS foods are date marked if being cold held for longer than 24 hours. Items must be discarded if not used within 7 days of preparation.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
The dish machine’s sanitizing concentration was tested at 0ppm (CL). Discussed with PIC and a technician will be contacted to service the machine. PIC stated that the facility has been having issues with the machine recently. The facility is instructed to use quaternary ammonia (available in house) to sanitize dishes until the dish machine is fixed. Ensure that the dish machine is functioning properly and testing at 100ppm (CL) to properly sanitize dishes. 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Date marking of TCS foods including but not limited to cheese, deli meats, and chicken were not observed during the inspection. Discussed date marking TCS food items with PIC. Ensure TCS food items stored in house longer than 24 hours are date marked and discarded if not used within 7 days. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Observed several dead bugs in the corners of the room to the left of the pizza oven. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that dead bugs are never present in the facility and are removed when cleaning occurs. 

6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Overall, the facility is need of a deep cleaning. Areas that are specified are as followed:
- the triple sink is observed to have dried food debris stuck to the basins of the sinks  
- the dish room was extremely accumulated with grease, food debris, etc.
- inside and out of the dish machine is heavily soiled with accumulation
- floors, walls, floor drains, and ceilings are accumulated with soil throughout the entire kitchen

Ensure that cleaning occurs as often as necessary to prevent accumulation. Suggest pulling equipment from wall (that has wheels) to throughly cleaning beneath and the back of equipment throughly. This also allows access to clean the wall behind the equipment as well. When closing occurs, be sure that employees are sweeping in areas of the facility where food preparation doesn’t occur such as the room to the left of the pizza oven and dish room. 

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.
